title: Responder handoff tray with cost & SLO micrograph attach flow
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: On-call handoffs in the Redwood Console lack a compact, actionable surface that combines the most urgent incident context (active alerts + recent SLO deltas) with immediate cost signals and a fast way to attach a postmortem draft or runbook snippets. Existing handoff surfaces either focus on long-form postmortems or ephemeral alert lists; engineers told us they need a minimal, scannable tray to pass baton during shift changes and urgent escalations.

Proposal: Introduce a 'Responder Handoff Tray' — a collapsible, right-rail tray that surfaces: top 3 active alerts, a micrograph row of SLO deltas (sparkline + percent delta), a rolling 24-hour cost delta card, and a quick-attach flow for postmortem/draft links and runbook snippets. The tray should support keyboard quick-open (shift+H), one-click copy of current alert links, and an inline ephemeral comment field that can be converted to a postmortem attachment.

User stories:
- As an on-call engineer, I want to quickly see which SLOs changed most in the past hour so I can prioritize triage.
- As a team lead doing handoffs, I want to add a short note and attach a draft postmortem link before leaving the shift.
- As an incident commander, I want to surface cost anomalies related to the incident to decide on fallback policies.

Acceptance criteria:
- Tray opens from any console page and anchors to the right column without obstructing primary console content.
- Shows top 3 alerts (title, severity, brief cause tag) linking to the alert thread.
- SLO micrograph row: each SLO shows a 6-point sparkline, current value, and +/− delta label.
- Cost card shows 24h delta, a sparkline, and a link to detailed cost breakdown.
- Quick-attach flow: paste link or choose from Drive/Confluence, optionally add a 280-char note, and press 'Attach & Notify' which creates a lightweight postmortem link in the alert thread.
- Keyboard shortcut opens/closes tray; tray state persisted per user session.

Constraints and tradeoffs:
- Keep visual weight low to avoid distracting from incident triage; use micrographs and condensed typography.
- Initial rollout will be read-only for cost details (click-through to full cost dashboard), to avoid permission complexity.
- Runbook attachments will store a reference URL rather than hosting content in Console to avoid storage/compliance work.

Design links and artifacts: See Figma prototype for interaction flows and accessibility states. Prototype includes dark/light tokens, 2 density modes, and a11y contrast checks.

Notes for engineering: Backend needs an API for SLO micrograph (6 point sample across short window) and an endpoint to create 'handoff attachments' referencing external links. Ensure attachments include minimal audit metadata: user, timestamp, source URL.

Release considerations: Flagged behind 'handoff-tray' feature flag. Initial GA in console-2026.03 after 2-week canary and accessibility sign-off.
design_notes: Key visual decisions: condensed list for alerts (max 3), color-coded SLO delta pills (red/orange/green), subtle gradient for cost sparkline to indicate anomaly when delta > 20%. Interaction: tray shallow slide-in, not modal; on mobile, collapses into a single icon that expands to full-screen handoff composer. Accessibility: ensure keyboard focus trap on attach flow, ARIA labels for sparklines, and text alternatives for color-only signals.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial problem framing and low-fidelity sketches uploaded to Figma. Held kickoff with ENG and PM; consensus to prioritize keyboard shortcut and cost delta.

2026-03-11 - Liam Chen: Added accessibility checklist and updated micrograph cadence to 6 samples (1 sample per 10 minutes for 1-hour window) to reduce noise. Asked for ENG API contract for SLO samples.
2026-03-12 - Maya Rodriguez (PM): Confirmed quick-attach should create a reference link in the alert thread and trigger a notification. Customer impact expected medium for teams using Dedicated.

2026-03-13 - Design critique notes: Reduce default tray height to 320px, move 'Attach & Notify' primary button to the right, add confirmation toast variant for failed attachments. Consider rate-limit UX for mass attachments.

2026-03-14 - Eng feedback (Evan Park): ENG-8420 will provide SLO micrograph API; need additional field for sample timestamps. Cost API will return 24h delta and 48h baseline. Blocking: authentication for Drive/Confluence pickers (work with Integrations team).

2026-03-15 - Usability test (3 participants): Handoff flow completed in average 22s; suggestions to shorten label copy and expose 'copy alert links' action more prominently. Updated prototype to include a single-action copy button.
